purpose: Bounded paired 100-update diagnostic of the pinned STE-FlowNet self-supervised photometric plus smoothness objective on the new ReplicaCAD shared bank.

model.name: STE-FlowNet
model.input: Pinned five-bin equal-event-count Gaussian representation per polarity; native 240x320, zero padded to 352x352.

data.gray_endpoints: Per-pixel linear luma 0.2126*R + 0.7152*G + 0.0722*B from the same registered Genesis float32 radiance frames at indices 0 and 3 (0ms and 30ms); no gamma inversion or per-frame fitting.
data.paired_event_representation_and_labels: Same physical rollout, shared 30ms flow and visibility-valid mask; generator-specific event tensors only.

training.sampling: At each of 25 cycles, a seeded permutation of the four complete training rollouts; same rollout order for both arms.
training.augmentation: disabled to isolate the registered one-window-per-rollout inputs; identical preprocessing and no event-count-based sampling.
training.padding: Events zero padded to 352x352; endpoint grayscale replicate padded from native 240x320 to 352x352. Output is cropped back to native coordinates for EPE.
training.objective: Pinned STE-FlowNet four-scale Charbonnier photometric loss plus 10x pinned second-order smoothness; uses the existing objective_dt1 helper and align_corners compatibility patch without changing loss code.
training.stop_rule: Exactly 100 optimizer updates per arm; fail on nonfinite objective/gradient, zero gradient, nonadvancing Adam step, or unequal initialization.

evaluation.masks: Same shared GT validity and pre-frozen union of nonzero normal EventGenesis/V2E event support; full-valid and common-active EPE reported.
diagnostics: normal vs zero-event vs reversed-five-bin input
evaluation.perturbation_mask: Frozen from normal paired inputs; never recomputed after intervention.

interpretation_limits: Only four training and two independent validation rollouts, with one 30ms sample per rollout.
This diagnostic tests the original self-supervised optimization path; it is not a formal long training run or a generator superiority comparison.
Static-scene camera motion only; no moving-object or dynamic-occlusion supervision is represented.
A short training response does not establish generalization to MVSEC or any other real domain.
